text: What is the converse of the following assertion? "I stay only if you go"
options: If I do not stay then you go
If you do not go then I do not stay
If I stay then you go
answer: "I stay if you go" (i.e. Q→P, the converse of P→Q) - recorded on GATE Overflow as option (A) of the paper
solution: Let P = "I stay", Q = "you go". "P only if Q" ≡ P→Q. The converse of P→Q is Q→P = "If you go then I stay" = "I stay if you go". Caution: the option list mirrored on GATE Overflow places this text as its fourth item while the accepted answer calls it option (A); match by content, not by position.
